question.prompt: The equation \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{2x^2}{x-1}-\frac{2x+7}{3} &{}+\frac{4-6x}{x-1}\\ &{}+1=0 \end{aligned} \] can be transformed by eliminating fractions to the equation \(x^2-5x+4=0.\) The roots of the latter equation are \(4\) and \(1.\) Then the roots of the first equation are:

solutions.explanation:
The original equation contains the denominator \(x-1\), so it is defined only when \(x\ne1\). Clearing denominators can produce a polynomial equation that is also defined at an excluded value, so its roots must be checked against this restriction.

For \(x\ne1\), multiplication by \(3(x-1)\) is reversible and gives the stated quadratic after simplification. Its only roots are \(1\) and \(4\), so no other value can solve the original equation. Reject \(1\), since it makes an original denominator zero. At \(x=4\), the original left side is
\[
\frac{32}{3}-\frac{15}{3}-\frac{20}{3}+1=0.
\]
Therefore the original equation has only the root \(\boxed{4}\), choice C.
